Sheba son of Bichri
SHEE-buh son of BIK-rye
proper noun
Hebrew Sheba, perhaps “an oath” or “seven,” a Benjamite rebel against David.

📖 Biblical Definition

Sheba the son of Bichri was a man of Belial of the tribe of Benjamin, who raised a rebellion against David in the troubled days after Absalom’s revolt. He blew a trumpet and cried, “We have no part in David, neither have we inheritance in the son of Jesse: every man to his tents, O Israel” (2Sa 20:1), and the men of Israel went up from after David to follow Sheba, though Judah clave to the king. David sent Amasa, then Abishai and Joab, to pursue him; and Joab, having treacherously slain Amasa on the way, chased Sheba to the city of Abel of Beth-maachah and besieged it (2Sa 20:14–15). Then a wise woman of the city cried out to Joab, and learning that he sought only Sheba, she counselled the people in her wisdom; they cut off the head of Sheba the son of Bichri and cast it over the wall to Joab, who then blew the trumpet and withdrew (2Sa 20:22). So the rebellion ended with the rebel’s head. Sheba stands as a type of the seditious spirit that despises the LORD’s anointed and sows division among the people of God; his cry of “no part in David” was the very voice of rebellion, and it brought him to a swift and shameful end.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

A Benjamite who rebelled against David, crying “We have no part in David”; beheaded at Abel of Beth-maachah.

expand to see more

SHEBA THE SON OF BICHRI, a Benjamite, a man of Belial.

He raised a rebellion against David after Absalom’s revolt (2Sa 20:1).

He cried, “We have no part in David,” and Israel followed him.

Joab pursued him to Abel of Beth-maachah and besieged it (2Sa 20:15).

A wise woman of the city had his head cast over the wall (2Sa 20:22).

📖 Key Scripture

2Sa 20:1 — "And there happened to be there a man of Belial, whose name was Sheba, the son of Bichri, a Benjamite: and he blew a trumpet, and said, We have no part in David, neither have we inheritance in the son of Jesse: every man to his tents, O Israel."

2Sa 20:2 — "So every man of Israel went up from after David, and followed Sheba the son of Bichri: but the men of Judah clave unto their king, from Jordan even to Jerusalem."

2Sa 20:21 — "The matter is not so: but a man of mount Ephraim, Sheba the son of Bichri by name, hath lifted up his hand against the king, even against David: deliver him only, and I will depart from the city. And the woman said unto Joab, Behold, his head shall be thrown to thee over the wall."

2Sa 20:22 — "Then the woman went unto all the people in her wisdom. And they cut off the head of Sheba the son of Bichri, and cast it out to Joab. And he blew a trumpet, and they retired from the city, every man to his tent. And Joab returned to Jerusalem unto the king."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

A figure of Scripture, not a contested doctrine; he is a type of the seditious spirit that despises the LORD’s anointed.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the ruinous end of the seditious spirit. Sheba’s cry, “We have no part in David,” was the very voice of rebellion against the LORD’s anointed, and it sowed division among the people of God. Those who lift up their hand against God’s appointed order and stir up strife bring destruction upon themselves; Sheba’s rebellion ended with his own head cast over the wall.

The wise woman of Abel offers the brighter contrast. Where Sheba sowed strife, she sought peace, counselling the city to give up the one rebel rather than perish for his sake. Her wisdom saved a city. The Scripture honours the peacemaker who quiets sedition and spares the innocent, even as it shows the certain ruin of the man who sets himself against the throne of David, the type of Christ the King.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

The name perhaps means “an oath” or “seven,” borne by this Benjamite rebel.

expand to see more

Sheba — Hebrew Sheba, perhaps “an oath” or “seven.”

He was the son of Bichri, a Benjamite.

He is called a man of Belial, a worthless man.

He raised rebellion against David with a trumpet and a cry.

He was beheaded at Abel of Beth-maachah.

Usage

"Like Sheba, those who lift their hand against God’s anointed and sow strife bring ruin on themselves."

"Sheba teaches that the cry “no part in David” is the very voice of rebellion against the King."

"The wise woman of Abel, against Sheba, shows the honour of the peacemaker who quiets sedition."
